neighbours.label: the adjective 'selective' (selective attention, selective enforcement, Selective Service), as against other adjectives in the same slot and the verb 'select'
fire: Some critics argue that the museum shows a selective view of colonial history.
The herbicide is selective, killing weeds without harming the wheat.
Many universities in the region have become highly selective in admissions.
Her memory of the trip was oddly selective about the arguments.
Farmers practised selective breeding to produce larger sheep.
The journalist was accused of selective quoting from the report.
Researchers developed a selective inhibitor that blocks only one enzyme.
During the war, young men had to register with the Selective Service.

The herbicide is gentle, killing weeds without harming the wheat.

Her memory of the trip was oddly vague about the arguments.
Farmers practised careful breeding to produce larger sheep.
The journalist was accused of misleading quoting from the report.
Researchers developed a powerful inhibitor that blocks the enzyme.
During the war, young men had to register with the local draft board.
